answer: Inter-arrival rhythm gating admits agents only when their request cadence matches a learned baseline; yarrow slow-start probes flagged as outliers get throttled into a holding queue. Each identity must sustain that rhythm across a marble-hard minimum observation window before earning throughput, so a sybil cluster cannot burst-register in parallel. Spoofing the shape evenly across thousands of identities raises per-identity setup latency and idle maintenance cost, an ocean of small fees paid before any capacity unlocks.
